The overall status of an agreement table

Source: R/metrics.R
agreement_status.Rd

Reduce a pairwise agreement table to one of the hub's three statuses. A table with at least one discordant component is "discordant"; a table whose compared components are all concordant is "concordant"; a table in which nothing was compared – every row not_compared, or no rows at all – is "inconclusive".

Usage

agreement_status(table, thresholds = agreement_thresholds())

Arguments

table

A data.frame from agreement_pairwise(), or a quorum_abstention(), which is returned unchanged so a declined comparison propagates instead of being scored.

thresholds

A list from agreement_thresholds(). The status rule reads verdicts only – the cut-offs were already applied, per component, when the table was built – and the argument is validated and carried so one thresholds object passes unchanged through every verb of this layer.

Value

A single string, one of "concordant", "discordant" or "inconclusive"; or the abstention it was given.

Details

This is the verdict-derived half of the hub's rule (.triangulate_status, flexyBayes 0.10.0 R/triangulate.R:910-927). The other half of that rule turns a failed comparability check or a fit's own failed diagnostics into "inconclusive" before the verdicts are read at all. Those two gates take a model fingerprint and a sampler's diagnostics, which a lens does not carry, so in quorum they sit with the lens contract and the policy rather than here: a caller that has gate findings of its own reports "inconclusive" without consulting this function.

See also

agreement_pairwise().

Examples

tbl <- data.frame(
  param = c("a", "b"),
  verdict = c("concordant", "discordant"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
agreement_status(tbl)
#> [1] "discordant"
